title: Chicken Marsala With Pancetta
blurb: The pancetta fat left in the pan becomes the base for the Marsala, so the pork seasons the whole dish rather than just garnishing it. A cornstarch slurry at the end thickens the sauce more reliably than reduction alone.
steps: Coat a large skillet lightly with olive oil and set over medium-high heat. Add the pancetta and cook until it has rendered its fat and the pieces are crisp at the edges. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving every bit of the fat behind — that fat is the sauce's backbone, not a by-product.
Put the flour on a plate. Pat the cutlets dry, season lightly with salt and pepper, then dredge in the flour.

Heat the pan with the pancetta fat over medium-high heat, adding a touch more olive oil if needed to make about 2 tablespoons. When it shimmers, shake the excess flour off the cutlets and lay them in. Sauté, turning once, until browned on both sides — thin cutlets only need a few minutes per side. Remove the cutlets and pour off the excess fat.
With the pan still over medium-high heat, add the Marsala and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Cook until reduced by about a quarter.

Stir the cornstarch into the cold water until no grains are left, then stir the cream into the pan. Add the slurry a little at a time, letting it come back to a simmer between additions, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Adding it gradually matters — cornstarch sets as it heats, and a sauce taken too far can't be loosened back.
Return the chicken and pancetta to the pan, turning to coat, and reheat a minute. Serve with the sauce spooned over the top and a sprinkling of parsley.
